p: pride of thine heart hath deceived: Which despises all others in respect of yourself, and yet you are but a handful in comparison with others, and you are shut up among the hills as separate from the rest of the world.

If thieves came to thee: God will so destroy them that he will leave none, even though thieves when they come take but until they have enough, and they that gather grapes always leave some behind them. See Geneva "Jer 49:9"
have brought thee even to the: Those in whom you trusted to have help and friendship, will be your enemies and destroy you.
bread have laid a wound under: That is, your familiar friends and guests have by secret practices destroyed you.

brother Jacob shame shall cover thee: He shows the reason why the Edomites were so severely punished: that is, because they were enemies to his Church, whom he now comforts by punishing their enemies.

on the other side: When Nebuchadnezzar came against Jerusalem, you joined with him, and had part of the spoil, and so rejoiced when my people (that is, your brother), were afflicted, whereas you should have pitied and helped your brother.
a stranger: When the Lord deprived them of their former dignity, and delivered them to be carried into captivity.
of the LORD is near upon: When he will summon all the heathen, and send them to destroy you.
drunk upon my holy mountain: That is, rejoiced and triumphed.
as though they had not been: The Edomites will be utterly destroyed, and yet in spite of all the enemies I will reserve my Church and restore it.
a fire: God attributes this power to consume his enemies to his Church, which power properly belongs only to himself; Isa 10:17, De 4:24, He 12:29.

mount of Esau: He describes how the Church will be enlarged and have great possessions: but this is mainly accomplished under Christ, when that faithful are made heirs and lords of all things by him who is their head.
Canaanites: By the Canaanites, the Jews mean the Dutchmen, and by Zarephath, France, and by Sepharad, Spain.

saviours shall come up on mount: Meaning that God will raise up in his Church those who will rule and govern for the defence of it, and for the destruction of his enemies under the Messiah, whom the Prophet here calls the Lord and head of this kingdom.
